page: Amazon Web Services t3.2xlarge is a burstable general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 2.5 GHz, configured with 8 virtual CPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per virtual core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks reveal a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities under the burstable CPU allocation model. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25% and 10% respectively. However, multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth read/write speeds reach average tiers. The instance demonstrates average throughput in Redis SET operations and Passmark CPU encryption tests, but struggles with intensive tasks like bzip3 decompression and medium-sized LLM inference, which rank in the bottom 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the t3.2xlarge is designed for workloads with variable CPU utilization. The burstable credit model allows users to maintain a lower baseline cost while retaining the ability to burst to full CPU performance when demand spikes. This resource profile is best suited for general-purpose applications, development environments, low-to-medium traffic web servers, and background microservices that do not require sustained, high-performance compute or local storage.
